boundaries: Ideality (ideal gas, dilute solution, complete reaction as stated) is an applicability condition, never a universal claim.
Separate amount (mol) from mass, concentration from absolute amount, and gauge from absolute pressure.
No synthesis procedures, energetic-materials quantities, toxicology, exposure assessment or laboratory-safety advice.
Equilibrium constants and kinetics are deferred unless purely algebraic with explicit scope; record them as deferred with sources.
Reaction equations are transcribed exactly as given with source locators, never rebalanced silently.
coverage_guidance: Priorities are seeds, not a finite checklist. Continue into adjacent source chapters/subtopics inside the boundaries, selecting independently reusable relationships. Save multiple bounded batches without waiting for owner review. Check supplied inventory and prior returns for equivalent relationships and conflicting IDs. Record out-of-format discoveries as deferred with exact sources and missing capabilities; do not force chains or dilute quality for a quota.
integration_expectation: Pressure, temperature and amount-of-substance dimensions are unsupported: mark requires-extension with full SI units and dimensions preserved. Mole-fraction, ratio and dilution records are scalar and still validate numerically in the kit. Never relabel temperature as duration, pressure as force, or amount as mass to force execution.
mission: Curate atomic, reusable quantitative chemistry relationships: gas laws, mole/mass/count conversions, solution concentration and dilution, and stoichiometric ratios, each with explicit validity conditions. Continue through successive review batches during the sustained session; no reaction chain or laboratory use case is required. This is quantitative formalization, not laboratory instruction.
priorities: Ideal gas law relating pressure, volume, amount and temperature
Molar mass conversion between sample mass and amount
Molar concentration and the dilution relationship between two solution states
Mole-ratio stoichiometric conversion for a balanced reaction as given
Partial pressure and mole fraction for an ideal gas mixture
special_checks: Absolute temperature is required: reject Celsius inputs used silently as absolute temperature
Gas-constant value and units go through constants metadata with source and locator; check R unit consistency per reference
Reject zero-amount, zero-volume and zero-total-pressure denominators explicitly
Dilution references must conserve amount by independent recomputation, not by repeating the relationship

https://webbook.nist.gov -- NIST Chemistry WebBook for constant and data provenance where needed; navigate to the exact record
